summary: The milestone completed 5 experiments in 25.2 minutes, and 3 were compute-bound. The 25.14-minute Recovered three-family SOTA entrance proposal bank set the critical path; the available data does not explain its internal cost.
bottlenecks_identified: Recovered three-family SOTA entrance proposal bank consumed 25.14 of the 25.2 milestone minutes, but no phase-level data is available to explain why.
Disk-mtime reconstruction reports 3 experiments at 0.0 minutes, which prevents useful duration comparison at that resolution.
The GPU report is not correlated with experiment execution windows, so it cannot establish utilization efficiency during compute-bound work.
No launch evidence records parallel model count and runner selection, so a missed DualGPURunner dispatch cannot be identified.
improvements_suggested: Record experiment start and stop times plus phase-level durations instead of relying on disk-mtime reconstruction.
Attach task-window GPU utilization samples to each compute-bound experiment.
Emit launch receipts with model count and selected runner, and use DualGPURunner when 2 or more models are loaded in parallel.
Profile the Recovered three-family SOTA entrance proposal bank before selecting a targeted optimization.
top_3_highest_leverage_actions: Add phase-level timers to the 25.14-minute critical-path experiment.
Correlate GPU telemetry with every compute-bound experiment window.
Record model count and runner selection at launch, with conditional DualGPURunner dispatch for 2 or more parallel models.
meta_reflection: The evidence localizes the critical path but does not reveal its cause. The GPU snapshot is not task-correlated, and no launch record establishes a 2-or-more-model workload, so neither compute-window efficiency nor a DualGPURunner miss can be claimed; synthesis-only GPU idleness is not a defect.
